name: Achenseebahn
kurzbeschreibung: The Achensee Railway, steaming since 1889 as Europe's oldest purely steam-operated cog railway, ascends steeply from Jenbach to the sparkling shores of Lake Achensee.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Achensee Railway (Achenseebahn) stands as an internationally renowned jewel of railway heritage: inaugurated in June 1889, this narrow-gauge railway (1,000 mm gauge) has steamed continuously from the Inn Valley up to Lake Achensee, claiming distinction as Europe's oldest cogwheel railway operating entirely with steam traction. Tracing a scenic 6.8-kilometre route, the nostalgic train masters a vertical rise of 440 metres between Jenbach railway station (530 m) and the Seespitz lake terminal (963 m). The engineering core is a 3.5-kilometre mountain section utilizing the Riggenbach rack system, where authentic 19th-century steam engines—including named locomotives 'Theodor', 'Hanna', and 'Georg'—push vintage open-air passenger carriages up gradients reaching sixteen percent. The hiss of steam and magnificent overlooks down into the Inn Valley evoke the golden dawn of alpine tourism.

Route & Anforderungen

Riding the Achenseebahn is a captivating outing for train enthusiasts, families, and sightseers. Departing Jenbach, the locomotive pushes the coaches through fragrant mountain woodlands and stone rock cuts along the cog railway section up to Eben station. Here, the locomotive uncouples, maneuvers around the train, and pulls the carriages across the level adhesion section through the pastures of Maurach to Seespitz. Total travel time is approximately 45 minutes. Open-sided summer carriages maximize alpine vistas and photographic angles. Historic baggage compartments accommodate folded strollers and wheelchairs. Wearing weather-appropriate layers is recommended, as passing breezes and harmless soot specks are part of the authentic steam train atmosphere.

Besuch & Anreise

The journey commences at Jenbach station in the Inn Valley, a major ÖBB rail hub served directly by Austrian Railjet and regional express lines. Drivers will find public parking at Jenbach station as well as at Seespitz. At the lakeside terminus in Seespitz, passengers enjoy a seamless cross-platform connection directly onto the decks of Achensee passenger ships.

Tipps

Secure a seat on an open carriage platform to fully experience the evocative aroma of coal smoke and panoramic mountain vistas. The combined 'Cog Railway & Boat' ticket offers the quintessential vintage day trip pairing mountain steam with lake cruising.
preis: Fares apply (combined tickets with Achensee boat cruises available)
oeffnungszeiten: Operates daily May to late October according to seasonal schedule
